opened_locators: Section4, equations(4.11)–(4.14), printed pp.422–424; searchable text774–893
Theorem(4.14), printed p.423 (PDF p.19), original formula visually checked
exact_source_check_records.scope: For a parallelism on a (4k-1)-manifold the original real Adams invariant is epsilon(k) times the reduced Dirac eta invariant minus its connection transgression. The exact coefficient is epsilon(k)=1/2 for k odd. On the flat Lie-framed T3, k=1, the connection term is zero, paired Fourier eigenvalues give eta=0, and periodic spinors have complex dimension2. Hence the real invariant is (1/2)(2/2)=1/2 modZ. The complex invariant alone would be0 and is not substituted for the real one.

opened_locators: Section4 Theorem(4.1), Corollaries(4.2)–(4.4), and complete printed proof, pp.76–78; text308–446
Original pp.76,77,79 visually opened, including the double-suspension relation at the start of p.79
exact_source_check_records.scope: Theorem4.1 gives [i_n,i_n]=2{h_n}-E(alpha_(n-1)); Corollary4.2 gives E2(alpha_(n-1))=2E{h_n}. Corollary4.3 states that some k-fold suspension pi6(S3)→pi(6+k)(S(3+k)), k>=2, is injective. These groups are in the stable range. Together with the separately opened pi6(S3)=Z/12 and stable pi3=Z/24 tables, the image is the unique order12 subgroup. Thus the order2 stable class12nu determines the unique order2 unstable class6nu-prime. The source convention for the Hopf map is explicitly stated on p.76.

opened_locators: TheoremII and its corollary, pp.314–315; text90–167
Original stable orthogonal period table, printed p.315 (PDF p.4), visually opened
exact_source_check_records.scope: The period for pi_k(O), k=0,...,7, is Z/2,Z/2,0,Z,0,0,0,Z. In positive degree SO has the same homotopy; the universal Spin cover removes pi1 and preserves groups of degree>=2. Hence the stable groups used in B1.1 are pi1Spin=pi2Spin=0, pi3Spin=Z, pi4Spin=0, and pi6SO=0. The six-sphere stable framing difference is zero, and the three-dimensional Spin comparison reduces to H3.

Its proof imports Krylov’s (YUY)^4 relation. B6.2 cites this as an example of the additional smooth identification that would be required by the abandoned plumbing approach; it does not apply the hypersurface theorem to the present torus family.

A proper holomorphic submersion with compact Kähler fibres over a small polydisc has a holomorphic Hodge-filtration period map in the locally constant marking. The locally simultaneous minimal elliptic pullbacks in B6.12 are smooth projective surfaces and therefore satisfy these hypotheses. Their finite deck characters define holomorphic eigensubbundles. Nonconstant period maps and exclusion of rational Hodge loci then use the separately computed hyperbolic monodromy and signatures.

receiving_read_records.scope: Full four proofs read and rederived, including free-circle conifold model, Jin invariant identification, spin trace, and actual cubic collar computation. Associated arithmetic reruns pass.

The actual quotient is S2xS3, spin and simply connected with no torsion in homology. Preserving the primitive circle Euler class and orientation makes the return Torelli. The source is an isotopy classification, using Lemma2.1, not merely a rational characteristic detection. Its primitive and doubled-sphere twists have (cube,p1*x)=(1,4),(8,8). Thus their bordism coordinates ((4k-ell)/24,k) are (0,1),(1,8), an integral basis; ell=-4 gives A+2B=-1 and k=-1+6B.
Exact inverse of the characteristic-number matrix with determinant-24 and the ell=-4 specialization. Does not evaluate the remaining integer B or prove Jin’s classification.

receiving_read_records.scope: Full four proofs read and rederived, including free-circle conifold model, Jin invariant identification, spin trace, and actual cubic collar computation. Associated arithmetic reruns pass.

The boundary is a closed spin7-manifold with torsion-free H4, and the actual Spin-c coboundary has a determinant class with a relative lift. With p1(boundary)=0 the source normalization is Z/28. Substituting p-hat=(p1+z^2)/2 and dividing by28 yields (p1^2-4sigma)/896-p1*z^2/192+z^4/384, exactly B6.9. Its relative products and the zero-shear case are verified in the receiving proofs; both spin lifts induce the same boundary Spin-c structure when H2 vanishes.

The boundary is a closed spin7-manifold with torsion-free H4, and the actual Spin-c coboundary has a determinant class with a relative lift. With p1(boundary)=0 the source normalization is Z/28. Its relative products and the zero-shear case are verified in the receiving proofs; both spin lifts induce the same boundary Spin-c structure when H2 vanishes.

exact_source_check_records.scope: Proposition8.3.5 makes E1^(p,q)=H^q(X_p,Z)⇒H^(p+q)(X_bullet,Z) a spectral sequence of mixed Hodge structures for a separated simplicial scheme. At C3=0 the finite 2Z3 toroidal cover has smooth projective toric strata and algebraic face maps. Add the degenerate simplices to the finite normalization semisimplicial scheme; its normalized alternating complex is unchanged. Each H^q(stratum,Q) is pure of weightq, so E2^(p,q) is pure of weightq. For r>=2 the differential changes q to q-r+1 and is therefore zero. Finite deck invariants are exact overQ. The explicitly computed integral E2 groups are free, so rational vanishing implies integral vanishing inductively, and extensions of free abelian groups remain free.

opened_locators: Author manuscript dated September1,2021, title page
TheoremA and surrounding hypotheses pp.2–3; TheoremB p.4, exact sequence visually verified
exact_source_check_records.scope: E1.3 uses the C3=0 family after the finite deck-lattice cover 2Z^3. The already printed properness proof and unimodular toric charts give a proper holomorphic map, smooth away from0, with smooth total space and SNC central fibre. The strictly coherent positive quadratic function Q=4 sum n_i^2-(sum n_i)^2 supplies a relative projective polarization, hence a Kähler total space over the disc. These are Chen’s exact hypotheses. Complex surjectivity onto monodromy invariants implies rational surjectivity by scalar extension; finite deck invariants are exact over Q.

receiving_read_records.scope: Full proofs of listed statements read except the still unresolved geometric d2 identification in F.2.6. Exact matrix, discriminant, period and LSAP-tube programs pass. The actual LSAP bundle-section theorem, Nagy inertia theorem and Jin statements have been opened.

The printed spanning tubes supply LSAP, and Proposition7.13(d), rather than the unresolved general Oka-1 fibre-bundle question7.10, supplies the section theorem. For F3.10 the vertical spray dominates on the attaching discs away from the finite fixed-jet set, exactly as in5.6–5.8. At a critical arc the compact set has the Mergelyan property; the fixed jet points lie in its interior. After a holomorphic frame is chosen, Theorem2.13 applies to Grassmannian-valued maps, leaving the base coordinate fixed.

The frame bundle over the open Riemann surface is a holomorphic submersion over a Stein base with fibre GL(n,C). Its global vertical spray is (g,A)→g exp(A), and its derivative is onto the vertical tangent. A complex bundle over a graph has a continuous frame because GL(n,C) is connected. Theorem1.2 deforms that section to a holomorphic frame, which is the only use in F3.10.
